title: AP Investigation: ICE Body Camera Policy Restricts Footage Release to Agency's 'Best Interests'
excerpt: An Associated Press investigation revealed that ICE's new body camera policy, adopted as the agency rushed to deploy cameras following two fatal agent-involved shootings without cameras, gives ICE broad control over public disclosure—specifying that footage from deaths or serious injuries will be released only when deemed in the 'best interests of the agency.'
content:
On August 7, 2026, the Associated Press reported on ICE's new body-worn camera policy, which governs how footage will be made public after the agency began a nationwide rollout following the fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine—neither of which was captured by cameras.

The policy specifies that ICE will release footage from shootings and other encounters in which agents cause death or serious injury only after determining "it is in the best interests of the agency" to do so—a provision critics said could allow officials to indefinitely withhold accountability footage.

  • Congress had provided ICE $20 million for body cameras in April 2026. ICE spent $30.9 million in July—beginning one day after the fatal Maine shooting—to purchase equipment from Axon.
  • ICE said cameras had been sent to more than half its field offices, with the rest to receive them by end of September 2026, pushing back earlier promised deadlines.
  • ICE's sister agency, CBP, had not released footage of the January 2026 fatal shooting of U.S. citizen Alex Pretti in Minneapolis, even though cameras were present, months after the incident.
  • At least one member of every arrest team is required to have a camera, the agency said, but the policy's public-release provisions drew bipartisan criticism from Congress.
The agency's body-worn camera policy "could mean taxpayers who are pitching in tens of millions of dollars to pay for the cameras may be kept in the dark about some high-profile confrontations." — Associated Press
